name: Central Luzon
subtitle: The rice belt
question: When the rains shift, what happens to the rice fields?
description: Follow the seasonal rhythm of flooded paddies, planting and crop growth across the Central Luzon plain.
hypothesis: A rainfall deficit may delay field flooding or planting. A changing HH/HV signal could reveal a shift in the crop cycle.
evidence: Compare same-track radar acquisitions with rainfall, crop calendars and field observations. A single dark pixel is not evidence of drought.
disprove: Normal planting dates and irrigation deliveries, or changes explained by harvest, would weaken the rainfall explanation.
humanDrivers: Irrigation schedules, crop choice, harvest and changes in land use also reshape the radar signal.
selectionNote: Prompt study box; retained only with real intersecting GCOV footprints.

name: Angat reservoir
subtitle: A changing shoreline
question: How much of the shoreline moves between observations?
description: Track the footprint of open water in the reservoir and compare it with rainfall in its catchment.
hypothesis: Lower rainfall may reduce inflow and expose the shoreline. Reservoir operations may produce the same pattern.
evidence: Look for persistent, spatially connected changes along the shoreline. Compare with official water levels and rainfall. Surface area is not water volume.
disprove: Stable or rising water levels, or a documented release explaining the drawdown, would weaken a drought explanation.
humanDrivers: Dam releases, water abstraction and irrigation allocations can outweigh the rainfall signal.
selectionNote: Angat uses the existing reservoir-centered box; the supplied 121.4 E center is east of this reservoir.

name: Dadu, Sindh
subtitle: Reading a floodplain
question: Can radar separate new floodwater from permanent water?
description: Use historical flooding as a method test, then apply the same questions to new radar observations.
hypothesis: New connected low-backscatter areas may indicate open floodwater, if rainfall and independent imagery support the interpretation.
evidence: Compare pre-event and post-event Sentinel-1 or compatible NISAR scenes, permanent water, elevation and rainfall.
disprove: Radar shadow, dry smooth soil or unchanged permanent water would contradict an open-floodwater interpretation.
humanDrivers: Embankments, drainage, canal operations and settlement patterns influence where water collects. The 2022 flood is a historical test, not evidence for a 2026 El Niño impact.
selectionNote: Prompt study box; retained only with real intersecting GCOV footprints.

name: Lower Piura
subtitle: A Pacific floodplain
question: Does surface water expand on the Piura floodplain?
description: A coastal Peru site for testing seasonal water change, subject to the timing of the local rainy season.
hypothesis: Extra seasonal rain can coincide with Pacific warming. Coastal SST, local rainfall and river operations must support this interpretation.
evidence: Same-track water masks, rainfall and independent river or flood observations; a seasonal baseline is needed.
disprove: No rainfall increase, stable river levels, or irrigation explaining the signal would weaken the hypothesis.
humanDrivers: Irrigation, levees, reservoir releases and land use can change surface water.
selectionNote: Prompt study box; retained only with real intersecting GCOV footprints.
